scenarios.name: gateway-model-and-mcp
assertions: The model request uses the configured HELM /v1/responses route and an episode token supplied by core.
The live local HELM MCP connection uses header-helper Authorization, with no static or OAuth credential taking precedence.
An expired or stopped core session cannot continue using a gateway model or effect route.
The effective requirements retain the provider pin and forbid danger-full-access.

scenarios.name: managed-observation-consumer-contract
assertions: The effective PreToolUse and PostToolUse commands invoke shared core observe with the original hook JSON stdin unchanged, and are asynchronous.
The synchronous PreToolUse deny remains separate from shared observe and returns no submission or persistence claim.
Shared observe exits zero with empty stdout on malformed input, no episode, rejected post or transport failure; no exit is counted as proof of delivery.
CP ingestion/readback establishes persistence; core status supplies diagnostics, and coverage stays observed-only.
All helpers in a session use the same distinct HELM_EXECUTOR_SLOT; no adapter reads, parses or writes core credentials or state files.

scenarios.name: governed-push-pr-escalated-merge
assertions: Raw push, merge, kubectl, flux and direct Linear writes are locally denied and hook actions are observed-only.
A governed push and PR creation dispatch only after a gateway ALLOW.
An ESCALATE merge does not dispatch until the designated owner approves the same intent and expected head.
The merged head and merge SHA are read back from the gateway-owned effect observation.
Actual sandbox traffic cannot reach direct GitHub or Linear write endpoints; template inspection alone is insufficient.

scenarios.name: claude-code-to-codex-switch
assertions: Core stop in the first session precedes Codex checkout of the same CP work-item UUID in a distinct HELM_EXECUTOR_SLOT; CP allows one live episode per work item and can retain a 409 hold until the last token expires and attempts are read back.
Existing attempts, UNKNOWN states and holds survive the executor switch.
Stopping the old episode does not cancel or reissue the underlying effect.

scenarios.name: D8-lost-tool-response
assertions: Inject loss after the provider applies the effect but before the first tool response is delivered.
Retry the same canonical target and intent from Codex, including after switching from Claude Code.
Effect identity remains derived from work_item_id, effect_type, canonical target and intent digest; never from hook call, request or episode ids.
The retry resolves to the same attempt and causes no second provider dispatch.
Reconciliation establishes the external result before accepting the work; UNKNOWN is not counted as success.

unit_test_limit: Unit tests use synthetic events and a command fixture. The integration runner uses actual core plus its fake CP/gateway; both cover bounded local behavior, never deployed gateway/CP or native Kernel conformance.
